To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a robust computationally-efficient nonparametric cyclic spectrum sensing method for cognitive radios, and we establish its asymptotic distribution and show that it can be used for cyclostationary signal detection.
a robust computationally-efficient nonparametric cyclic-correlation-based spectrum sensing method is proposed and its theoretical properties and performance are investigated.

a nonparametric robust cyclic correlation estimator is proposed, its asymptotic distribution under the null hypothesis and a robust spectrum sensing test are derived, a sequential spectrum sensing scheme for reducing the detection time is proposed, and the proposed nonparametrical cyclic correlation-based spectrum sensing method is shown to be reliable and highly robust in both Gaussian and heavy-tailed noise environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of robust nonparametric spectrum-sensing algorithms based on the spatial sign function and its application to cognitive radio systems.
the problem of spectrum sensing and detection of cyclostationary (CS) signals in the presence of heavy-tailed noise.
the development of robust nonparametric spectrum detection methods for cognitive radio systems operating in challenging environments with unknown noise statistics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed nonparametricspectrum sensing method is highly reliable and robust in both Gaussian and heavy-tailed noise environments.

the proposed nonparametic cyclic correlation based spectrum sensing method has superior robust performance in both Gaussian and heavy-tailed noise environments compared to the conventional cyclostationary signal detection methods.
the spatial sign cyclic spectrum sensing is a very robust method for spectrum sensing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel and computationally efficient non-parametric method for spectrum sensing in cognitive radios.

the nonparametric cyclic-correlation-based spectrum sensing method is a robust and computationally efficient spectrum sensing method that is applicable for both single-user and collaborative cognitive radio networks.
nonparametric statistics provide an additional robustness against non-Gaussian noise and when the exact noise distribution is unknown.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nonparametric cyclic spectrum sensing method based on the spatial sign function provides reliable detection of cyclostationary signal even when the noise is heavy-tailed and the noise statistics are unknown.
nonparametric spectrum sensors are robust to heavy-tailed noise, and they are computationally efficient, which is an important advantage over parametric spectrum sensors.
nonparametric cyclic correlations can be used for reliable spectrum sensing in challenging environments.
